narr: Southerly flow as well as intermittent showers and a few thunderstorms raised the dew point into the mid 60s to around 70 across the area. Also, forecast soundings showed a very moist and deep warm layer up to around 12,000 feet. This combined with strong 850mb moisture convergence across southern Missouri and Illinois and precipitable water values in the 99th plus percentile, set the region up for a heavy rain and flash flood event. Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.
ev: Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time onto already saturated soil. This caused flash flooding. In Cuba, the viaduct near the railroad tracks flooded. Also, portions of Highway 19 and Route PP were flooded. Sections of Highway N southeast of Bourbon were impassable. A number of low water crossings and roads in the Leasburg area were flooded and the water was several feet deep in these locations.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time onto already saturated soil. This caused flash flooding. Many small creeks were flooded across northern portions of the county. Also, several low water crossings and roads had several feet of water over them, especially in the Richwoods area.

Up to three inches of rain fell in a short amount of time onto already saturated soil. This caused flash flooding. In Fletcher, Calico Creek rose well out of its banks flooding Calico Creek Road, Old Highway H and Nickelson Road. The intersection of Highways Y and C in front of Grandview High School was flooded. A number of roads in the De Soto area had several feet of water over them. Larry G. Crites Memorial Park, northwest of Festus, was flooded due to Joachim Creek.
